title: Per-entity baseline scorecard — user account, SSH auth-rate feature
event_type: Baseline-lookup scorecard view for one entity/feature pair (analogous to DET-31-01's ssh_auth_baseline.csv row plus the current hour's scored observation)

fields.label: staleness_check
fields.value: fresh — last rebuild 11h ago, on schedule

callouts.explanation: The raw count being scored this hour — on its own, too low to trip any fixed-threshold rule, which is exactly the case this part's machinery exists to catch.
The learned normal range for this specific entity and hour, not a global constant — the same seven attempts would score very differently against a noisier account's baseline.
The number that actually drives the alert decision; this is what turns 'seven attempts' into a claim about how unusual seven attempts is for this account.
The field named in §1's Engineering Reality box and §9's closing paragraph — without a visible staleness check, a scorecard built from six-week-old history looks identical to a fresh one.

note: Illustrative/conceptual rendering of what a per-entity baseline scorecard's fields would contain; not a captured screenshot of any UEBA or analytics product interface.
